note: An ear game of the wide leaps up from Do: the two 6ths, the two 7ths and the octave, each answer button named with its plain meaning the first time, and the why says how to tell them apart (how far each stops short of the high Do). One feel to reach, no count.

exercise.title: 6ths, 7ths or octave?
exercise.why: The 6ths, the 7ths and the octave land on notes next to each other under the high Do, so you can name each leap by how far it stops short of the octave.

cells.text:
Press Start below to hear the first question: the game plays Do, then a note a 6th, a 7th or an octave above it.
Hum the second note back. Then pick its name: m6 for the minor 6th, M6 for the major 6th, m7 for the minor 7th, M7 for the major 7th, P8 for the octave, and press Next below for another leap.
Practice until you hear the high Do in your head before you pick, and each answer is a step down from it.
